skill.name: tool-presets

remediation.suggestion: Add a short least-privilege warning before recommending all tools for comprehensive agents.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Tool Access Guidance

content.value_statement: Agent tool access can vary across similar roles, creating inconsistent workflows. This skill documents reusable Claude Code presets for development, analysis, research, and coordination agents.
actual_capabilities: Lists six named tool presets and their included tool sets.
Explains when to choose development, file operations, analysis, research, orchestration, and full-stack presets.
Provides a frontmatter example for applying a preset pattern to an agent definition.
Documents separate reference files for development, file operations, analysis, research, and orchestration presets.
Identifies example agent roles that fit each detailed preset.
limitations: Does not enforce permissions or update agent files automatically.
Does not include executable scripts or runtime validation.
Full-stack guidance is broad and should be reviewed before use.
Preset names still require tool names to be copied into each agent definition.

use_cases.title: Configure Developer Agents
use_cases.description: Choose consistent tool access for agents that write code, run tests, and handle build tasks.

use_cases.title: Document Agent Standards
use_cases.description: Create a shared reference for teams that maintain several Claude Code agent definitions.

use_cases.title: Review Tool Access
use_cases.description: Compare preset choices before granting Bash, web access, write access, or coordination tools.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Preset
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one new agent
prompt_templates.prompt: I am creating a Claude Code agent for documentation updates. Use the tool-presets skill to recommend the best preset and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Preset
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a preset pattern to an agent definition
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tool-presets skill to update my agent plan with the right tools for code refactoring without shell execution.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Access Levels
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare dev-tools, file-ops, and analysis for a code review agent. Recommend the least privileged preset that still supports the work.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tool-presets skill to build a permission matrix for developer, reviewer, researcher, and coordinator agents across our team.

output_examples.input: Select a preset for an agent that edits documentation and searches files.
output_examples.output: Recommended preset: file-ops. It supports reading, writing, editing, and search without shell execution.

output_examples.input: Compare dev-tools and analysis for a static review agent.
output_examples.output: Use analysis when the agent needs read-only search plus diagnostic commands. Use dev-tools only when the agent must modify code.

output_examples.input: Plan presets for a research coordinator.
output: Research worker: research preset for web and source gathering.
Coordinator: orchestration preset for task planning and delegation.
Reviewer: analysis preset for checking source material and results.

best_practices: Select the least capable preset that can complete the agent task.
Review Bash, WebSearch, WebFetch, and Task access before copying a preset.
Document the reason for each preset choice in the agent definition.
anti_patterns: Assigning full-stack to every agent for convenience.
Giving Bash access to agents that only need read-only analysis.
Treating preset documentation as permission enforcement.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation for choosing tool sets and does not run commands by itself.

faq.question: Which tools does the dev-tools preset include?
faq.answer: It includes Read, Write, Edit, and Bash for agents that need development and test workflows.

faq.question: When should I use file-ops?
faq.answer: Use file-ops for file edits, search, refactoring, and documentation updates that do not need shell execution.

faq.question: Is full-stack safe for every agent?
faq.answer: No. Full-stack is broad and should be reserved for agents that truly need all capabilities.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, but the content is written around Claude Code tool names.

faq.question: Does the skill validate my agent configuration?
faq.answer: No. It provides preset guidance. You still need to review the final tool list before use.
